record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: For generalized tiling billiards in periodic polygonal tilings of the plane with Snell refraction coefficient -1, is there a finite list of generic dynamical archetypes, such as dense behavior in open sets and integrable behavior with periodic or linearly escaping trajectories?

evidence.quote: Is there a finite number of such archetypal behaviors?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a periodic polygonal tiling of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, in which the plane is partitioned into polygonal cells whose collection is invariant under a lattice $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ of translations. A generalized tiling billiard trajectory is a piecewise-linear oriented curve in $\mathbb{R}^2$ that moves along straight segments inside each cell and, upon crossing an edge $e$ shared by two adjacent cells, refracts according to Snell's law with refraction coefficient $-1$: if $\theta$ is the angle that the incoming segment makes with $e$, the outgoing segment makes angle $-\theta$ with $e$ (equivalently, the refracted ray is the reflection of the incoming ray with respect to the edge $e$, but continuing into the neighboring cell rather than bouncing back).

A trajectory is called:
- periodic if it is a closed curve;
- linearly escaping (drift-periodic) if it is invariant under a non-trivial translation of $\Lambda$ and escapes to infinity;
- dense in an open set $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ if its closure contains $U$.

Call a "generic dynamical archetype" for a given periodic polygonal tiling a qualitative description of the asymptotic behavior of trajectories that holds for a full-measure (or otherwise generic) set of initial conditions; examples include "every generic trajectory is periodic", "every generic trajectory is linearly escaping", or "the closure of a generic trajectory contains an open set".

Question: As the periodic polygonal tiling of the plane varies over all such tilings, does the collection of generic dynamical archetypes that occur for generalized tiling billiards with Snell refraction coefficient $-1$ form a finite list?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (2024–2025) on generalized tiling billiards in cyclic polygons and wind-tree variants establish dynamical results for specific tiling families (triangles, cyclic quadrilaterals) but explicitly note that a general theory is lacking. No source indicates a proven finite classification of generic dynamical archetypes for arbitrary periodic polygonal tilings, so the problem appears open.

status_evidence.title: Deviations for Generalized Tiling Billiards in Cyclic Polygons
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work explores generalized tiling billiards in special families (cyclic polygons), proving deviation results but not a general archetype classification.
status_evidence.claim: General classification of archetypes for arbitrary periodic tilings has not been established; current results address specific families.

status_evidence.title: Negative refraction and tiling billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces tiling billiards with refraction coefficient -1; describes behaviors (periodic, drift-periodic, exceptional Rauzy-like) only in particular tilings.
status_evidence.claim: Archetypes are described case-by-case; no finite list across all periodic tilings is proven.
